newsitem.title: USA: Zaire rebel needs democratic "seasoning" - U.S.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel needs democratic "seasoning" - U.S.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Bill Richardson said on Sunday that Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila will need "seasoning in the democratic process" to be an effective government leader.
"The jury is still out on Kabila," Richardson said on the CNN programme "Late Edition."

"He is street smart, he's pragmatic, he's obviously a good military fighter. But we're concerned that the way he's dealt with refugees, with some of the human rights reports, that he needs a lot of seasoning in the democratic process," Richardson said.

Richardson, who was in Zaire last week to try to help ease control of the country from its embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko, said he felt there was a "good chance it will be a peaceful transition" to a new government.
Mobuto and Kabilia are scheduled to meet on Wednesday, which Richardson said he hoped would ease the shift of power and prevent the looting of the capitol city, Kinshasa.
Rebels surround Kinshasa, but Richardson said he did not feel international citizens in the city were in serious danger.
Richardson has said that because of Kabila's military victories, there was a good chance he would replace the long-time dictator Mobuto, who is ill with cancer.

"It's very important that Zaire be managed and governed democratically, that he have market reforms, that he institute human rights processes, that he deal with the refugees," Richardson said of Kabila.
